newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura punishment seen in few days after July 24.
newsitem.headline: Nomura punishment seen in few days after July 24.

text.p: Administrative penalties against scandal-hit Nomura Securities Co Ltd is likely to be announced within a few days after Nomura presents its case to the Ministry of Finance (MOF), financial industry sources said on Friday.
Earlier on Friday, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said MOF would ask Nomura to present its case on July 24.

The hearing, in line with government procedures, is to give Nomura an opportunity to explain itself over the case after Japan's securities watchdog recommended to MOF that it impose penalties against Nomura earlier this week.

Sources said that after the hearing from Nomura, which they expect will be attended by Nomura President Junichi Ujiie, the ministry will, during the following few days, make a final decision on penalties against the brokerage.

The penalties are not expected to take effect immediately as the top Japanese brokerage will be provided with time to notify its customers, the sources said. Some sources said MOF's penalties may not take effect for about one month.
A Finance Ministry official said that MOF has not decided when it will announce its penalties against Nomura.
